tool_input.command: grep -niE "version|release" CONTRIBUTING.md README.md | head -30; grep -niE "decision|policy" docs/doc.md CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md | head; git log --all --oneline | head; git notes list 2>/dev/null | head

mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/version-scheme.md <<'EOF'
# Version numbering scheme

The project's current recorded decision is to number releases using semantic versioning (semver).
EOF
cat docs/policies/version-scheme.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/version-scheme.md`. It says the project's current recorded decision is semantic versioning (semver). It doesn't mention the retired alternative.

The decision comes from claude-mem's prompt history, and nothing in the repo records a version policy. There, an earlier prompt said "calver" and a later one said "semver". I treated the later one as the current decision. Both were bare one-word prompts, so I have no rationale or rules for the file, and I didn't invent any. The file's only source is that single prompt, and it's in the search results under "General" rather than under a gin project.

The repo is consistent with semver. `version.go` sets `Version = "v1.12.0"`, but that isn't a written policy. If you want the file to rest on something more durable, the decision should also be recorded in the repo, for example in CONTRIBUTING.md.
